original_question: Let N be a complete hyperbolic 3-manifold with fundamental group generated by n elements, and consider its convex core. Is there a universal upper bound R_n, depending only on n, for the radius of any embedded ball entirely contained in the convex core of N?
target_in_paper: The draft targets the unnumbered Question in the section titled "Convex hyperbolic 3-manifolds," which asks whether, for a complete hyperbolic 3-manifold N whose fundamental group can be generated by n elements, there is an upper bound R_n (depending only on n) for the radius of an embedded ball entirely contained in the convex core of N.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual wording. It correctly identifies the ambient object (a complete hyperbolic 3-manifold N), the hypothesis on the number of generators of π1(N), the geometric locus of interest (the convex core), and the exact type of bound being asked for: an n-dependent upper bound on the radius of an embedded ball contained in that convex core.
missing_details: The paper's nearby context defines the convex core using a Kleinian presentation N = H^3/Γ: it is the quotient of the convex hull of the limit set of Γ. Making that definition explicit makes the question fully stand-alone.

The quantifiers should be stated explicitly: for each integer n >= 1, does there exist a constant R_n < infinity such that every complete hyperbolic 3-manifold N with π1(N) generated by n elements satisfies the bound?
To avoid ambiguity, "generated by n elements" should be phrased as "can be generated by n elements" (equivalently, rank at most n), rather than exactly n generators.
It is helpful to specify that the radius is measured in the hyperbolic metric, and that an "embedded ball" means an embedded hyperbolic metric ball lying entirely in C(N).

The original question is stated with no extra restrictions such as quasifuchsianity, compactness of the convex core, or absence of cusps; a stand-alone rewrite should preserve that generality and not add such assumptions.
refined_question: For each integer n >= 1, does there exist a constant R_n < infinity, depending only on n, such that whenever N = H^3/Γ is a complete hyperbolic 3-manifold whose fundamental group π1(N) can be generated by n elements, every embedded hyperbolic ball contained entirely in the convex core C(N) — where C(N) is the quotient by Γ of the convex hull of the limit set of Γ — has radius at most R_n?
justification: The paper states this as an unnumbered Question, not as a numbered conjecture or theorem. Your draft already matches that question almost verbatim. The only substantive additions needed for a fully stand-alone, paper-faithful formulation are the explicit quantifiers over n and N, the standard definition of the convex core from the immediately preceding context, and the clarification that the radius is the hyperbolic metric radius of an embedded ball contained in C(N).
